fields.label: Dust Particle Concentration
fields.help: Enter the concentration of dust particles in the air compartments. Valid values are >= 0. The default value of 6.15E-08 is the value used for California residential sites by version 1.5 of the CalTOX model (see Table VI of: CalEPA (California Environmental Protection Agency), Department of Toxic Substances Control. 1993. Parameter Values and Ranges for CalTOX. Draft (July). Available online from a university at: https://emhea.uta.cloud/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/CalTOX_Parameter-values-and-ranges.pdf.)

fields.label: Density of Air (g/cm<sup>3</sup>)
fields.help: Enter the density of air in the air compartments. Valid values are >= 0. The default value of 0.0012 (1.19E-03) is from Table B-1 of U.S. EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency). 1997. Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment. EPA-452/R-97-005. Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards and Office of Research and Development. December. Available online at: https://www3.epa.gov/ttn/atw/112nmerc/volume3.pdf.

fields.label: Default Height of Air Volume Elements (m)
fields.help: Enter the default height of air volume elements. Valid values are >= 20. The default value of 226 is a health-protective choice from: approximately the 5th percentile of median hourly mixing heights, derived from data at 824 meteorological stations paired with upper-air stations across the United States from January 1–December 31, 2016. You may later override this value using site-specific a single value or a time series of mixing heights.

fields.label: Density of Dust Particles (kg/cm<sup>3</sup>)
fields.help: Enter the density of dust particles in the air compartments. Valid values are >= 0. The default value of 1400 (1.4 g/cm<sup>3</sup>)  is from Page 2 of Bidleman, T.F. 1988. Atmospheric processes. Environmental Science and Technology 22:361-367.

fields.label: Fraction Organic Matter of Dust Particles
fields.help: Enter the fraction organic matter of dust particles in the air compartments. Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.2 (20%) is from page 1601 of Harner, T., and Bidleman, T.F. 1998. Octanol-air partition coefficient for describing particle/gas partitioning of aromatic compounds in urban air. Environmental Science and Technology 32:1494‑1502.

fields.label: Surface Soil Tilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of a tilled layer of surface soil. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.20 is from Human Health Risk Assessment Protocol for Hazardous Waste Combustion Facilities (including the Hazardous Waste Companion Database of chemical-specific parameter values). U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Solid Waste and Emergency Response, Washington, DC. EPA-530-R-05-006. September. Available online at: https://archive.epa.gov/epawaste/hazard/tsd/td/web/html/risk.html.

fields.label: Surface Soil Untilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of an untilled layer of surface soil. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.01 is from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk..

fields.label: Root Soil Tilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of a tilled layer of root-zone soil. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.60 assumes that the total thickness of the surface-soil layer and root-zone layer is 0.8 (0.01 for untilled surface soil [from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.] + 0.79 for untilled root zone [from Table 16 - U.S. Average from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk]). If the thickness of a tilled surface soil layer is 0.2 (from Human Health Risk Assessment Protocol for Hazardous Waste Combustion Facilities (including the Hazardous Waste Companion Database of chemical-specific parameter values). U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Solid Waste and Emergency Response, Washington, DC. EPA-530-R-05-006. September. Available online at: https://archive.epa.gov/epawaste/hazard/tsd/td/web/html/risk.html.), then the thickness of a tilled root zone is 0.8-0.2=0.6.

fields.label: Root Soil Untilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of an untilled layer of root-zone soil. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.79 is from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.

fields.label: Vadose Zone Soil Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the vadose zone. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 1.4 is from Table 17 - U.S. Average from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.

fields.label: Groundwater Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the groundwater layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 3 is from Table 3 - Thickness of the aquifer layer from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.
